title: Prompting for Better Results
summary: Practical techniques for writing prompts that produce useful, accurate and well-structured outputs for everyday financial services tasks.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Practical techniques for writing prompts that produce useful, accurate and well-structured outputs for everyday financial services tasks.
Learning Objectives: Write clear prompts with context, role, task and format
Refine outputs through iteration and follow-up instructions
Build reusable prompts for common work tasks
Syllabus: Anatomy of a good prompt: context, task, constraints and output
Iterating, critiquing and asking the model to check its work
Prompt patterns for summaries, drafting, comparison and analysis
Intended Audience: Staff at all levels who use or plan to use generative AI tools in their work
Front-office, operations, compliance, risk and support teams adopting approved AI tools
Managers responsible for supervising AI use within their teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior experience of AI is required. Familiarity with the firm's approved tools and AI policy is helpful.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
IOSCO, The Use of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning by Market Intermediaries and Asset Managers (2021)
